title: Agent Architectures & Cognitive ReAct Loops
description: Understand AI agent cognitive architecture, the ReAct reasoning-action pattern, working memory, and tool integration in .NET.

data.text: From Stateless Prompts to Autonomous Agents

A standard LLM completion is purely reactive: you submit an input, the model generates an output, and execution stops. An AI Agent, by contrast, possesses agency: it is endowed with goals, short-term memory, an action space (tools), and an autonomous decision loop. The agent evaluates the current environment, reasons about what steps are necessary to reach its objective, executes external tools, observes the results, and iterates until the goal is satisfied.

data.caption: The ReAct (Reason + Act + Observe) Agent Cognitive Architecture
data.definition:
graph TD
    Goal["User Objective: 'Audit customer account #892 and refund overcharges'"] --> Brain["Agent Brain (LLM Reasoning State)"]
    Brain --> Thought["1. Thought: 'I need to fetch recent transactions first.'"]
    Thought --> Action["2. Action: CallTool('GetTransactions', { customerId: 892 })"]
    Action --> Environment["External World: CRM / Database / Stripe"]
    Environment --> Observation["3. Observation: 'Found 2 duplicate charges of $49.00'"]
    Observation --> Brain
    Brain --> NextThought["4. Next Thought: 'Overcharges confirmed. I will issue a refund.'"]
    NextThought --> NextAction["5. Action: CallTool('IssueRefund', { amount: 98.00 })"]
    NextAction --> FinalResult["6. Completed Goal Response to User"]

data.text: The Four Pillars of Agent Architecture

rows: Ingests user prompts, file attachments, and environmental webhooks
ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs, SSE, Channels
Must sanitize user inputs to prevent prompt injection
Deconstructs complex goals, decides tool selection and parameters
Must enforce bounded loop limits (e.g. max 10 steps)
Maintains conversational history (short-term) and recalled facts (long-term)
Must prune context window to prevent token exhaustion
Interacts with external databases, APIs, code interpreters, and file systems
Must enforce granular permissions and authorization checks

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Agents move beyond stateless prompts to autonomous loops: Reason -> Act -> Observe
The ReAct pattern grounds reasoning in verifiable observations returned by tools
Agent systems require four core pillars: Perception, Brain, Memory, and Action space
Always guard autonomous loops with iteration limits (MaxIterations) to prevent infinite loops
Enterprise agents must maintain an auditable transcript of internal thoughts and tool calls
data.takeaway: Agent fundamentals center on controlled iterative execution. Equipping an LLM with structured tools and a bounded ReAct loop empowers it to perform complex multi-step enterprise workflows.
